questions.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-{105}^{∘}={30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x={30}^{∘}$ and $y={135}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $\frac{5\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{6}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{12})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $\frac{11\pi }{12}=\frac{7\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}.$*
questions.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{4}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})?$
questions.worked_solution:
The angle ${75}^{∘}$ is not a special angle. However, we can rewrite it as the sum of two special angles, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{75}^{∘}={45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We now recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x={45}^{∘}$ and $y={30}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the exact value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$ without using a calculator.

*Hint: Use the fact that $\dfrac{\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}.$*
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(x-y) = \sin x\cos y - \cos x\sin y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $y = \dfrac{\pi}{4},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\sin\left(x - 30^{\circ} \right )$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u-v) = \sin u\cos v - \cos u\sin v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v=30^{\circ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{30}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u+v) = \sin{u}\cos{v} + \cos{u}\sin{v}
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
